title: The Vishnu Smriti — the Sanskrit text
dateDisplay: c. 3rd century BCE–3rd century CE (date unsettled)
attributionNote: A dharma text transmitted without an author's name, taught in it by Vishnu himself to the goddess of the earth: the rules of conduct and penance that a Vaishnava household kept. Different from the four dharma sutras in that its aphorisms are set out in verse, and later in date. GRETIL's e-text follows the edition of V. Krishnamacharya (Madras 1964, Adyar Library Series 93, 1–2), whose commentary by Nandapaṇḍita is not part of the file, and was input by I. Shima.
description: The Viṣṇusmṛti sets out the duties of the castes and the stages of life, the sacraments of birth, initiation, marriage and death, the law of the king and of the court, the rules of purification and the penances that expiate each offence, fasting, pilgrimage, the gifts owed to Brahmins, and the worship of Vishnu. It is the most orderly of the smritis, arranged in a hundred adhyāyas whose verses were chanted and cited in the ritual digests of south India.
historicalContext: Composed for the Vaishnava communities of the late ancient period, the text belongs with the Puranas and the sectarian dharmas that shaped the practice of temple and household; it was carried to the West by Julius Jolly's translation, which the library holds as The Institutes of Vishnu.
availabilityNote: Complete as GRETIL publishes it: all 100 adhyāyas and 2,854 verses, streamed from GRETIL at read time, one chapter at a time. The commentary printed with the edition is not part of the e-text. This is the original Sanskrit, not a translation.
